      - paragraph: 11 regions ↔ 11 vertices. 17 shared borders ↔ 17 edges.
    - article:
      - heading "Quick facts" [level=2]
      - paragraph:
        - img
        - text: At most four colors suffice for every planar map under shared-edge adjacency.
      - paragraph:
        - img
        - text: Appel and Haken announced the computer-assisted proof in 1976.
      - paragraph:
        - img
        - text: The proof reduces the problem to an unavoidable set of configurations.
      - paragraph:
        - img
        - text: Reducibility rules these configurations out of a minimal counterexample.
    - article:
      - heading "Common misconception" [level=2]
      - paragraph: Touching at a point does not require different colors.

    - article:
      - heading "Theorem statement" [level=2]
      - paragraph: Every planar map can be colored using at most four colors so that no two regions sharing an edge have the same color.
      - paragraph: This map can also use three colors. The theorem gives an upper bound, not a requirement to use all four.
    - article:
      - heading "About the proof" [level=2]
      - paragraph: The accepted proof is computer-assisted. Finite configuration checks belong to a broader mathematical argument, not merely a trial on a few maps.
